# MiniModel.MiRust.com Full Agent Context

MiniModel.MiRust.com is the developer documentation site for MiniModel.com. It serves documentation, schemas, examples, metadata guidance, and agent orientation only.

MiniModel.com is a Rust-first metadata and verification layer for tiny local AI model packages. It is not a model host, byte relay, or inference service.

## Hard Boundary

- Project servers never run user model bytes.
- Project servers never serve user model bytes.
- Project servers never proxy external model-byte downloads.
- TinyRustLM.com remains browser-local.
- Users import local `.slm` files through the browser file picker.
- Rust owns `.slm` validation, manifest verification, chunk verification, and import receipts.

MiniModel.com may publish static docs, schemas, example manifests, metadata-only catalog entries, public-key routes, signed catalog snapshots, model-card/license metadata, peer-source announcement feeds, and takedown/contact routes.

MiniModel.com must not publish third-party `.slm`, safetensors, GGUF, ONNX, adapter, tokenizer, or other runnable model bytes.

## `.slm` Summary

`.slm` v1 is TinyRustLM's local model format:

- little-endian
- magic `SLM1`
- version `1`
- 108-byte minimum header
- checksum field at bytes 100..108
- file checksum treats bytes 100..108 as zero
- 64-byte tensor directory entries
- 64-byte aligned tensor directory and tensor payloads
- supported dtypes: f32, q8_0, q4_0
- tokenizer sections: `BTOK` or `BPE1`
- tied output: `flags & 1 != 0`

The parser rejects bad magic, short files, unsupported versions, zero checksums, checksum drift, zero dimensions, invalid attention shapes, offset escapes, malformed tokenizers, unsupported dtypes, payload length drift, malformed quantization scales, duplicate tensor hashes, missing tensors, and output-head contract drift.

## Manifest v0

The manifest is line-oriented `key=value` text. It binds model id, publisher identity, model-card route, license route, artifact kind, artifact byte count, artifact SHA256, source identity, `.slm` format version, model shape, quantization, tokenizer checksum, tensor-layout checksum, runtime compatibility, evidence routes/checksums, source lane, chunk/Merkle fields, and signature fields.

`artifact.project_server_url` must be `none`. A manifest is not a fetch instruction. The user must provide local bytes or a consenting peer source.

## Verifier MVP

Implemented in MiniModel.org source:

- `minimodel-core`: parser, boundary checks, SHA256, chunk/Merkle verification, TinyRustLM `.slm` validation, peer-piece export/reassembly, and receipt writing.
- `minimodel`: CLI wrapper.

Important commands:

```text
minimodel verify-manifest <manifest>
minimodel verify-artifact <manifest> <artifact.slm>
minimodel write-import-receipt <manifest> <artifact.slm> <receipt>
minimodel prepare-peer-share <artifact.slm> <share-dir> <model-id> [source-huggingface-model-id] [known-peer-base-url]
minimodel serve-peer-pieces <manifest> <piece-dir> <bind-addr>
minimodel fetch-peer-pieces <manifest> <peer-base-url> <output-dir>
minimodel assemble-peer-pieces <manifest> <piece-dir> <output.slm>
minimodel import-peer-request <request-json> <manifest> <output-dir>
```

Catalog/availability commands include `write-catalog-entry`, `add-peer-source`, `write-peer-source-announcement`, `apply-peer-source-announcements`, `write-peer-source-announcement-feed`, `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcement-feed`, `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements`, and `write-catalog-snapshot`.

## Source Lanes

Local files:

- user supplies local `.slm`
- verifier checks local file
- TinyRustLM opens local file through file picker

Hugging Face:

- external metadata and user-side acquisition context only
- model cards, license routes, source revisions, file hints, and endpoint awareness are allowed
- local conversion request JSON and local `.tinyrustlm-convert.ps1` handoffs are allowed
- scripts run `convert-huggingface-request` against user-owned local `.safetensors`
- no project-owned tokens
- no project proxying of `/resolve/`
- no project hosting of converted bytes

P2P:

- current bridge is direct known-peer serve/fetch/import
- peer-source rows and announcement feeds are metadata only
- chunks are model bytes and must not be uploaded to project servers
- Rust re-verifies before TinyRustLM import
- local receipt comes before browser execution

## Optional Peer Companion

The MiniModel Peer Companion is future user-run local software for advanced peer duties: local peer identity, local piece stores, cache quotas, consent prompts, serve/fetch controls, import receipts, logs, and TinyRustLM handoff.

It is roadmap only. It must reuse shared Rust verifier crates and command contracts. Tauri v2, Iced, Slint, egui, Dioxus, Iroh/QUIC, Rust-libp2p, WebRTC, WebTransport, BitTorrent-style chunking, Pear, Bare, and Hypercore remain evaluation lanes until they preserve consent, local verification, and no-server-byte rules.

## Legal And Consent

MiniModel listings are publisher assertions, not endorsements. MiniModel does not certify safety, legality, training cleanliness, license validity, fitness for purpose, or output correctness.

Required gates:

1. Transfer consent.
2. Execution/import consent.

Publish takedown/contact routes before public submissions or peer exchange.

## Agent Rules

- Keep docs current before deploy.
- Do not expose credentials.
- Do not add model-byte hosting.
- Do not add automatic model fetches.
- Keep long-term memory pointer-based and checksum-bearing.
- Run relevant pointer audits and `git diff --check`.
